accepts.because: redraw against a fresh picture of the colony NOW, rather than at the next tick; the hive ticks on its own, this is the extra one

emits.because: the drawn page, for the browser that asked -- it leaves on the marked egress and never through a parent edge

description.purpose: One interactive canvas served over HTTP under the render cell's own path, drawing whatever its store holds. The first thing it draws is the colony itself. THE HIVE IS THE ADDRESS: `params.ports` is empty, so no edge reaches a cell in here; a caller names the hive and a lane on `hop.route`.
description.use_when: An operator or a user should see and rearrange something the colony knows, in a browser, without an operator UI release for every new kind of object. Nothing has to point at it -- the way in is the HTTP route.
description.not_in_scope: It draws nothing the store does not hold. The topology snapshot arrives on a timer through this hive's own `./probe -> /colony/graph` lane (GH #163: `/colony/graph` is one of the absolute endpoints a mutation may draw, because it is the colony's read-only topology endpoint and the sanctioned alternative to reading `colony.db`; the counts-never-content `/colony/ledger` joined it with GH #267). No realtime push (a viewer sees a change when it joins or interacts, not when another viewer moves a box). No object library beyond cells, hives and edges.
examples: GET /surface/org/acme/member/alice/canvy/render -> the colony as boxes and lines, draggable
refresh (timer) -> probe -> /colony/graph -> probe -> store: one snapshot row
socket event node:moved -> render -> store -> render -> the browser
description.contract_in: One lane, at the hive path. in_refresh -- take the topology snapshot now instead of at the next tick. Which cell does the asking is this hive's business.
description.contract_out: One lane, out of the hive path. surface -- the drawn page, carried by the marked egress back to the browser that asked. A parent draws no edge for it.
